document.title: Shell text uses the Runtime Default Font
document.summary: The VitaDeck Shell, the loading lines and the Deck App failure screen draw through `text_draw` with the Runtime Default Font instead of raylib's `DrawText`, and `bootstrap_draw_deck_canvas` uploads new glyphs every frame so that text appears without a running Deck App.
document.why: The Shell drew with raylib's built-in bitmap font, so it [could not render non-ASCII Deck App names or link labels and looked different from Deck Apps](source:s1).

sources.label: Claude Code session · Nov 5
sources.gist: Máté asks to move Shell DrawText/MeasureText calls (and the bootstrap startup/error screens) onto text_draw with the Runtime Default Font, keep layout equivalent, keep the raylib fallback, and not touch the Deck App render path.

sources.label: PR #149
sources.title: feat(shell): Shell text uses the Runtime Default Font, so non-ASCII names render

groups.title: Glyph upload every frame, and the bootstrap screens
groups.why: Glyphs only reached the GPU inside `render_draw_list`, which runs only while a Deck App is ready, so Shell text drawn without one would never appear. The startup and failure screens were [in scope](source:s1) too.
groups.summary: `bootstrap_draw_deck_canvas` now starts the text frame and uploads dirty atlas pages before anything draws, and the splash, loading line and failure screen draw through `text_draw`, with failure lines wrapped by `text_cluster_width` instead of per-byte `MeasureText`.

attention.note: Glyphs the Shell or the failure screen cache while drawing upload at the top of the next frame, so a first-seen string shows one frame late. With a ready Deck App, `text_begin_frame` now runs twice per frame (here and in `render_draw_list`), which keeps `src/ui/render.c` untouched; nothing caches glyphs between the two calls.

notes.body: The splash is a single frame before the main loop, so it follows the full measure, upload, draw protocol from `text.h` to show at all.
Breaking per cluster keeps multi-byte UTF-8 and emoji whole; the old loop split bytes.

fileNotes.src/core/bootstrap.c: Per-frame glyph upload; splash, loading and failure screen use `text_draw`.
fileNotes.tests/fixtures/golden/Linux/14-failure-s: Failure screen golden regenerated with DejaVu Sans.

groups.title: Shell draws through text_draw
groups.why: This is the [asked change](source:s1): Shell text through `text_draw` with the Runtime Default Font, layout kept equivalent.
groups.summary: Three static helpers in `shell.c` (`shell_text`, `shell_text_width`, `shell_text_y`) replace every `DrawText`/`MeasureText` call one to one, and `shell_text_y` centres a line in a row by `text_line_height` rather than the font size.

notes.body: DejaVu Sans' line box at 18 px is about 21 px, taller than the font size, so centring by the line height matches how `render_button_instance` centres Button labels.

fileNotes.src/shell/shell.c: All Shell text calls move to the new helpers; constants unchanged.
fileNotes.tests/shell_input_harness.c: Defines the stb_ds implementation, since `shell.c` now links `text.c`.

commits.subject: feat(shell): draw Shell text with the Runtime Default Font
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The Shell and the startup and failure screens drew with raylib's built-in
bitmap font, so they could not show non-ASCII Deck App names or Host Control
Link names. They now draw through text_draw with the Runtime Default Font,
which still falls back to raylib's font when it was not downloaded.
